rule.title: State and local taxes are limited to $40,000 ($20,000 MFS), reduced above $500,000 ($250,000 MFS) of MAGI

citation.wording: The overall limit on the deduction for state and local income, sales, and property taxes has increased to $40,000 ($20,000 if married filing separately). The overall limit is reduced if your modified adjusted gross income is more than $500,000 ($250,000 if married filing separately) but will not be reduced below $10,000 ($5,000 if married filing separately).

rule.open_point: Married filing separately follows the 2025 State and Local Tax Deduction Worksheet (spec 080 clarify Q4): line 1 'Enter $40,000', line 5 'Enter $500,000 ($250,000 if married filing separately)', line 7 'Multiply line 6 by 30% (0.30)', line 9 'Enter the larger of the amount on line 8 or $10,000', line 10 'Enter the smaller of the amount on line 9 (half the amount on line 9 if married filing separately) or the amount from Schedule A, line 5d'. Halving line 9 makes the MFS limit $20,000 less 15% of MAGI over $250,000, never below $5,000 — the 0.15 declared here is the worksheet's 30% halved by its line 10, not a printed rate. The statute as quoted reduces the MFS limit by 30% of the excess; the CPA decides. The MAGI the preparer enters must be the worksheet's line 4: Form 1040 line 11b plus excluded Puerto Rico income and Form 2555 lines 45 and 50 and Form 4563 line 15.
